items.prompt: Roads between towns have travel times (all positive). Find the fastest travel time from the capital to every town.
items.why: Weighted, non-negative edges, single source → Dijkstra with a min-heap. BFS counts edges, not minutes.

items.prompt: In a maze grid, find the fewest moves from the entrance to the exit (every move costs one).
items.why: All edges cost the same → BFS gives the shortest path in O(V + E). Dijkstra would only add a log factor.

items.prompt: Find the cheapest flight route from A to B that uses at most k connections.
items.why: Weighted path with an edge limit → Bellman-Ford for k + 1 rounds (relaxing from a copy), or Dijkstra over (city, stops).

items.prompt: Currency exchange rates are given; decide whether some sequence of trades returns more money than you started with.
items.why: Use log-weights −log(rate); a profitable loop is a negative cycle → Bellman-Ford detects it on the V-th round.

items.prompt: Tasks have durations and dependencies (no cycles). Find the earliest time all tasks can finish if independent tasks run in parallel.
items.why: A DAG and a longest (critical) path → process the nodes in topological order with a DP. Dijkstra can't maximise.

items.prompt: Connect all houses with pipes at minimum total cost, given the cost of a pipe between every pair.
items.why: A minimum spanning tree (Kruskal: sorted edges + union-find) minimises the total cost of connecting everyone, not the distance between two points.

items.prompt: On a height map, find a route from the top-left to the bottom-right that minimises the largest height difference between consecutive cells.
items.why: The path cost max(|Δh|) never decreases as the path grows → Dijkstra with max instead of +. A DP fails because moves go in all four directions (cycles).

items.prompt: Each grid cell is free (0) or a wall you may break (1). Find the fewest walls to break to cross the grid.
items.why: Edge weights are 0 or 1 → 0-1 BFS with a deque (Dijkstra's special case), O(V + E). Plain BFS treats all moves as equal and gets it wrong.
